key_insight: Twisted, coherently bonded lithium niobate interfaces form nanoscale structural helices separated by screw dislocations, with torsional strain implying accompanying dipolar helices.
engineering_relevance: Coupled plastic and elastic deformation at bonded ferroelectric interfaces offers a route to chiral oxide architectures distinct from moiré-based van der Waals twistronics.
method: Map interface contrast using 4D STEM and differential phase contrast.
Model electron channeling along helical paths and directly image structural helices using electron ptychography.
Assess chirality through sample-inversion imaging and second-harmonic optical circular dichroism.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports directly imaged structural helices, unchanged DPC images after sample inversion, and unusually large interfacial optical circular-dichroism signals.
watch_item: Dipolar helices are inferred from electromechanical coupling rather than directly imaged, and the abstract does not establish fabrication scalability.
